summary: Check whether two binary trees are structurally identical with equal node values.
mainInsight: Two trees are the same iff their roots have equal values and their left subtrees and right subtrees are the same - a simultaneous recursion with the base case that two empty trees are equal and exactly one empty tree is not.

approaches.name: Simultaneous recursion
approaches.summary: Compare roots, recurse on children pairs.

personalSolution.notes: Correct. Check the root values first and short-circuit to avoid needless recursion.

promptVariants: How do you traverse two trees in lockstep?
cards.explanation: Equality is structural: roots, left subtrees and right subtrees must all match.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Count the nodes: Equal counts do not imply equal shape or values.

promptVariants: What are the three base cases of Same Tree?
cards.answer: Both empty -> equal; exactly one empty -> not equal; both non-empty -> compare values and recurse. As soon as a value mismatch or an empty/non-empty pair occurs the answer is False, so there is no need to explore the rest of the trees.
cards.explanation: Short-circuiting saves work on mismatching trees.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Time complexity (n nodes): ___
cards.explanation: Each pair of nodes is compared at most once.

promptVariants: What is the space for balanced vs skewed trees?
cards.answer: The height h: O(log n) for balanced trees and O(n) for skewed trees.

promptVariants: Your code recurses on both subtrees before comparing p.val and q.val. Why is that wasteful and how would you reorder it?
cards.code:
sameLeft = self.isSameTree(p.left, q.left)
sameRight = self.isSameTree(p.right, q.right)
return sameLeft and sameRight and p.val == q.val
cards.answer: It evaluates both full subtree comparisons even when the root values already differ. Check the values first and return early: `if p.val != q.val: return False`, then `return self.isSameTree(p.left, q.left) and self.isSameTree(p.right, q.right)` (the second call is skipped when the first is False).
cards.explanation: Same worst-case big-O, much faster on mismatches.

promptVariants: What should isSameTree(None, None) and isSameTree(node, None) return?
cards.explanation: Two empty trees are identical; an empty and a non-empty tree are not.

incorrectOptionExplanations.True and True: A non-empty tree differs from an empty one.
